# Final upper documentation and authoring review

**Reviewer:** `final_docs`
**Exact upper revision:** `4008f4984ad0e6fc26d7fd1c1e3d6ca28673cc41`
**Lower base:** `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42`
**Read-only clone:** `/private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper-r4`

**Documentation verdict: APPROVE. Requirements verdict: PASS within this documentation, actual-template-authoring, and blast-radius lens. Independent core-fit verdict: PASS.** No reproducible correctness/documented-behavior mismatch remains in the cases reviewed. These are bounded code/documentation verdicts, not a claim that publication, CI, or every other S3 requirement is complete.

## Findings closed by observed behavior and honest guidance

The original ordinary-contraction defect remains fixed. The retained actual-template replay passes **9 of 9** cases on each supported Python version: the wrapped `Don't … don't` quotation and its exact-ASCII/curly-apostrophe controls work across decision, clarification, and review forms.

The later P3 documentation overpromise is also resolved. `templates/README.md` now explicitly says that literal recognition is lexical, explains the exact `R's release preserves users' work.` ambiguity, warns that rewrapping can produce an advisory, and gives the exact-spacing/line-break fallback. The skill reference and queue-writing scenario consistently describe presentation changes outside **recognized literal text**. The templates route authors through that canonical copy-and-fill guide. This correction does not imply a more permissive runtime.

I replayed the prior R-prefixed prose examples through coherent, real copied templates on both Python versions. **9 of 9 expectations pass per version:** the three wrapped-R cases still produce the now-documented advisory, while six exact-R and wrapped-Rust controls pass without source findings. The preserved original r3 probes expected the wrapped-R cases to pass under the old wording; the r4 copies explicitly expect an advisory under the corrected wording. Earlier files and results were not changed.

The ambiguity's literal-protection controls also agree with the guide. For `.py` source `R's  release'`, both the exact and backticked-exact quotations pass; removing one internal space or replacing literal contents with `[...]` is rejected. The exact R-possessive prose excerpt passes. Together with the prose ambiguity controls, this is **7 of 7 expected outcomes on each interpreter**. The guide therefore describes a real conservative limit and a verified workaround, without weakening actual prefixed-string protection or promising a general prose/language parser.

## Selected, executed, and skipped evidence

All custom scripts are independent reviewer probes derived from my preserved earlier evidence. The fixture scripts read the real templates, fill concrete questions with distinct consequences, stage their artifacts in real scratch Git repositories, and run nine authoring checks: schema, name, location, human attention, fold shape, rendered record lines, swallowed fields, ordinary links, and explanation shape. They do not reuse the repository test helper's generic placeholder filler.

| Selected check | Python 3.14.6 executed/result | Python 3.9.6 executed/result | Skips |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Source and legal-timing copied-template cases | 21 / 21, all expected | 21 / 21, all expected | 0 |
| Original contraction copied-template replay | 9 / 9, all expected | 9 / 9, all expected | 0 |
| Documented R-prefix copied-template cases | 9 / 9, all expected | 9 / 9, all expected | 0 |
| Literal, emphasis, omission, and bounded-token scalar cases | 52 / 52, all expected | 52 / 52, all expected | 0 |
| Prefix ambiguity and actual raw-string controls | 7 / 7, all expected | 7 / 7, all expected | 0 |
| Exact-800, 801-word, and below-answer-background budget cases | 3 / 3, all expected | 3 / 3, all expected | 0 |
| Selected new repository regression methods | 6 / 6, all passed | 6 / 6, all passed | 0 |

That is **101 selected and executed custom case expectations per interpreter**, plus **6 selected and executed repository test methods per interpreter**, with zero skips. Expected source advisories in negative/limitation cases are not relabeled as clean output.

The tests cover both exact and legitimately reformatted excerpts; short altered quotations; heading and line selection; angle destinations containing spaces; no-source decision/clarification behavior and the separate local-review-target obligation; three legal delivery timings; literal spacing and ellipses; triple-quoted strings with embedded quotes; omission boundaries; and newer visible Unicode separators versus identifier/numeric continuations. These were targeted probes, not a replacement for the parent's full corpus and portability reviews.

## Blast radius and retained bindings

The only changed instruction/authoring surfaces in the r3-to-r4 delta are `skills/explain-to-human/reference.md`, `skills/explain-to-human/scenarios/queue-item.md`, and `templates/README.md`. The actual queue templates, applicable AGENTS contracts, existing human questions, and the skill entry point did not change in that delta.

The skill entry point and its live explanation-standard review file remain **2 of 2 byte-identical to original PR89 `f56084d`**. The stored review digest still matches the actual skill bytes. The real teaching quotation is **1 of 1 verbatim** in its selected repository section under the final runtime. Main `326d8ed5fa4f89eaa1402a54d8377dba5946be12` and the named lower base are ancestors of the final upper pin. Final HEAD verification returned the exact OID above and `git status --porcelain` returned empty output.

The new guide keeps external content explicitly unfetched/unverified and separates source matching from relevance/truth. It preserves advisory source findings, ordinary link checks, exact local-review evidence, and the known literal-recognition limit. I found no remaining overclaim in the changed guidance against the tested behavior.

## Exact commands, outputs, and environment

Environment: Darwin 25.5.0 arm64; Git 2.55.0; `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` 3.14.6; `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9.6. All new probes/fixtures/logs are under `/private/tmp/final-docs-upper-r4-*`; no supplied clone/index/configuration or earlier evidence was edited. The host printed Xcode filesystem/cache warnings while launching one Python 3.9 fixture run; both the fixtures and selected tests completed, with no failures or skips.

## Independent core fit and limits

**Core-fit reviewer: `final_docs`. Agent substitution: PASS. Provider substitution: PASS. Repository substitution: PASS.** The changes remain repository-local Markdown/Git/Python-stdlib behavior. They do not require a particular writing agent, external provider, product workflow, personal setup, or user-global state. Exact source excerpts and preservation of unanswered review obligations apply across adopted repositories. The documentation now states the lexical limit rather than weakening the check to hide it.

I used only the mechanically supplied inputs, my own prior probes/findings, and allowed code/contracts/templates/Git objects. I did not read worker reports or other reviewer verdicts, bootstrap or mutate the clone, run a browser-rendering check, duplicate the complete repository suites or historical corpus replay, audit the owner's checkout, create closing records, or check/publish actual PRs. Those parent-owned or separately reviewed obligations remain outside this approval. No subsequent revision is certified here.
